title: The tightly knit Kirby group and its music
summary: Hughes recalls John Kirby on German radio; Maxine says the group was tight and Charlie Shavers and Billy made arrangements.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well I have the very faintest recollection when I was growing up in the 1950's, being raised in (Wales, ?) except for an hour or so -- a week, come to listen to continental radio stations.
And I seemed to remember there was quite a bit of John Kirby music played on German jazz programs.
I wouldn't be a bit surprised.
And I have a feeling I heard

of yours, 'Drink To Me Only With Thine Eyes', and possibly 'Molly Malone.'

Well by this time, Kirby's group was a very tightly knit group. And they were very popular at the time. In fact, they were known as the biggest little band in America. And they were having tremendous success. And, of course, mostly their big numbers were classics. And Lou Singer was responsible for those arrangments along with Charlie.

Yes, Charlie. And Billy made some too. But it took a lot of research and, of course -- Lou Singer had access to this research by being at the publishing company. And they turned out their best stomper on those -- well at that time, those classics; 'Anitra's Dance', and all those things that they do.
